items.title: All The Destinations Delta Air Lines Is Flying Its Rare Boeing 767-400ERs To In 2026
items.summary: Currently, only United Airlines and Delta Air Lines operate the Boeing 767-400ER as a scheduled passenger aircraft, although a VIP-configured airframe also operates for the Bahrain Royal Flight (Bahrain Air Force). While the -400ER is now a previous-generation aircraft with relatively high fuel consumption, it remains competitive within the Delta and United ecosystems for several reasons.
items.t: All The Destinations Delta Air Lines Is Flying Its Rare Boeing 767-400ERs To In 2026

items.title: We Tracked 133 Diverted Flights In Two Weeks: Here’s Where They Ended Up
items.summary: Flight diversions are often treated as isolated incidents, but a closer look at two weeks of aviation activity reveals a much larger pattern. Between November 6 and 18, 133 flights diverted from their intended destinations, and several airports saw multiple waves of diversions within hours. Some aircraft landed relatively close to their original destinations, while others ended up thousands of kilometers away.
items.t: We Tracked 133 Diverted Flights In Two Weeks: Here’s Where They Ended Up

items.title: United Airlines Cancels 27 International Boeing 737 MAX Routes: See Full List Now
items.summary: United Airlines is one of the world's top operators of narrowbody twinjets from the Boeing 737 MAX family, with fleet data from ch-aviation showing it currently has 123 737 MAX 8s and 188 737 MAX 9s . Going forward, the Chicago-based US 'big three' legacy carrier and Star Alliance founding member is set to receive 35 more 737 MAX 9s as its mainline fleet modernizes.
items.t: United Airlines Cancels 27 International Boeing 737 MAX Routes: See Full List Now

items.title: Boeing's New Air Force One Still Hasn't Flown & Here's Why
items.summary: The Boeing 747 may have ended its commercial production run, but two of the most consequential examples ever built remain deep inside a modification program that has stretched years beyond its original timetable. Boeing’s two purpose-built VC-25B presidential aircraft, which are the long-awaited replacements for the US Air Force’s aging VC-25As, were originally expected to be delivered by the end of 2024. Instead, the first aircraft is now scheduled for roughly mid-2028, while the second is expected around mid-2029.
items.t: Boeing's New Air Force One Still Hasn't Flown & Here's Why

items.title: Why Boeing Built The 737 MAX With The Ability To Take Off Overweight, Even Though It Can't Legally & Operationally
items.summary: As with all other modern narrowbody aircraft, the Boeing 737 MAX offers a taxi allowance between its Maximum Takeoff Weight and its Maximum Taxi Weight. This is related to ensuring the aircraft can actually take off with its maximum fuel capacity (by weight) in edge cases, as well as being related to safety margins.
items.t: Why Boeing Built The 737 MAX With The Ability To Take Off Overweight, Even Though It Can't Legally & Operationally

items.title: Showers & Bars: The Onboard Spaces Only The Airbus A380 Offers
items.summary: The Airbus A380 Superjumbo is the world's only full two-decked passenger aircraft , and as such, it provides much more room for airlines to utilize for luxury spaces such as a bar, lounge, and showers. Still, a traveler from the past may be taken aback by how little luxury space the giant aircraft has. It is extremely rare in today's world for modern passenger airliners to have a significant amount of rest and recreation space, even though this was once the norm. In some ways, Emirates' configurations of the Superjumbo preserve a vestige of the past.
items.t: Showers & Bars: The Onboard Spaces Only The Airbus A380 Offers

items.title: Delta Weight-And-Balance Outage Triggers Atlanta Ground Stop Days Before Thanksgiving
items.summary: Delta Air Lines flights bound for Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL) were held at their departure airports on Sunday morning after an outage affected the carrier's weight-and-balance calculations. The issue led the Federal Aviation Administration ( FAA ) to issue a ground stop at Delta's request, affecting hundreds of flights and causing mounting delays.
items.t: Delta Weight-And-Balance Outage Triggers Atlanta Ground Stop Days Before Thanksgiving

items.title: Premium Upgrade? United Airlines Is Replacing Its Remaining Boeing 767s With 787 Dreamliners
items.summary: On September 8, 1982, United Airlines brought the Boeing 767 into commercial service, revolutionizing its long-haul network with a twin-engine aircraft that could safely operate transatlantic routes dominated by quadjets. The airline still uses 53 of these legacy twinjets to anchor its transatlantic network from Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR) and Washington Dulles International Airport (IAD) more than 40 years later. The current fleet consists of 16 stretched 767-400ER aircraft with an average age of 23 years and 37 older 767-300ER aircraft with an average age of 29.
items.t: Premium Upgrade? United Airlines Is Replacing Its Remaining Boeing 767s With 787 Dreamliners

items.title: Here's How Many B-21 Raiders Northrop Grumman Plans To Produce Annually
items.summary: The first example of the world's first 6th-generation stealth bomber is expected to be 'on the ramp' at Ellsworth Air Force Base sometime in 2027. The US Air Force's B-21 Raider, built by Northrop Grumman , is one of the most resounding successes in recent procurement history for the Department of Defense. Although no official number has been announced for annual production, the Pentagon has already granted a 25% funding increase to expedite initial production.
items.t: Here's How Many B-21 Raiders Northrop Grumman Plans To Produce Annually

items.title: Highest-Paying Airline Jobs: 5 Roles That Earn Six Figures Without Flying
items.summary: The aviation industry depends on far more than pilots and cabin crew to keep its aircraft flying and its global operations running smoothly. Behind every departure is a network of highly skilled professionals responsible for flight planning, aircraft maintenance, complex electronic systems, engineering, and the financial decisions that keep airlines competitive. Many of these essential roles take place well away from the passenger cabin, yet they offer rewarding career opportunities and considerable earning potential.
items.t: Highest-Paying Airline Jobs: 5 Roles That Earn Six Figures Without Flying

items.title: BepiColombo reaches Mercury orbit after nearly eight years in space
items.summary:
The European-Japanese BepiColombo mission has entered orbit around Mercury, completing a nearly eight-year journey to the Solar System’s innermost planet.

The European Space Agency (ESA) confirmed the successful orbital capture on November 21, 2026, after its mission control team received signals from the spacecraft and assessed the initial telemetry.

The manoeuvre involved firing four thrusters on ESA’s Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) to reduce the spacecraft’s speed enough for Mercury’s gravity to capture it. BepiColombo initially entered an elliptical polar orbit measuring approximately 590 by 11,640 kilometres.

Launched in October 2018, BepiColombo has travelled around 9.9 billion kilometres through the inner Solar System and completed nine planetary flybys: one of Earth, two of Venus and six of Mercury.

Two orbiters travelling together 

BepiColombo is a joint mission between ESA and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). It consists of two scientific spacecraft: ESA’s Mercury Planetary Orbiter and JAXA’s Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter, known as Mio.

The two orbiters are currently still connected and travelling together. Mio remains protected by a sunshield, while MPO is responsible for the spacecraft stack’s manoeuvres during the final stages of arrival.

The orbiters are scheduled to separate on December 9–10, 2026. Mio will then move into its planned orbit to study Mercury’s magnetic field and magnetosphere, while MPO will perform additional manoeuvres to reach its own final science orbit.

Once the two spacecraft are operating separately around…
items.t: BepiColombo reaches Mercury orbit after nearly eight years in space

items.title: Drones strike Russian military-linked cargo ship in Gulf of Finland
items.summary:
A Russian cargo ship linked to the country’s military logistics network caught fire after a drone attack in the Gulf of Finland on November 21, 2026. The damaged vessel drifted into Finnish territorial waters, where authorities coordinated a rescue and firefighting operation involving Finnish, Estonian and Russian units.

The ship, Sparta II, was sailing from St. Petersburg toward Russia’s Kaliningrad exclave when it was hit. Finnish military officials said Ukraine was likely behind the attack, although Kyiv had not publicly claimed responsibility.

Drone attack damages ship 

Finnish Defence Forces detected a drone attack against the Russian cargo vessel on November 21, 2026, west of Gogland Island in the eastern Gulf of Finland.

Estonia’s Police and Border Guard Board said the explosions occurred while the ship was in Estonia’s exclusive economic zone, outside its territorial waters, in an international shipping lane. Finnish authorities initially described the attack location as international waters.

Russian officials said two drones struck the vessel. Finnish authorities confirmed a drone attack but did not independently confirm the number of drones involved.

The strike damaged the ship and started a fire. The vessel subsequently lost its ability to maneuver and drifted north into Finnish waters, eventually anchoring off the coastal town of Loviisa.

The Sparta II is a Russian-flagged cargo ship associated with Oboronlogistika, a company that provides logistics services to Russia’s Ministry of Defence. The vessel is under US and Ukrainian sanctions and has…
items.t: Drones strike Russian military-linked cargo ship in Gulf of Finland

items.title: Belgian strike to disrupt flights at Brussels and Charleroi airports
items.summary:
Brussels Airport (BRU) expects major flight disruption on November 23, after some air traffic controllers at Belgian air navigation service provider skeyes announced they would join a national demonstration.

The airport said most arriving and departing flights will have to be cancelled because skeyes will not be able to provide normal air traffic control services during the action. The disruption is expected from 7 a.m. to 9 p.m. local time (6 a.m. – 8 p.m. UTC).

Skeyes unable to provide normal ATC services 

According to Skeyes, the expected number of staff would not be enough to safely handle regular air traffic during the strike. It will therefore temporarily suspend normal services at Belgian airports and in the airspace under its responsibility. Minimum services will be maintained for emergency and other safety-critical flights.

Brussels Airport said airlines will contact affected passengers directly. Flight cancellations will appear on the airport’s website once they have been registered by the carriers.

Charleroi Airport also expects flights to stop 

The disruption will also affect Brussels South Charleroi Airport (CRL), another major Belgian airport and an important base for low-cost airlines.

Charleroi Airport said no flights will be able to take off or land between 7 a.m. and 9 p.m. on the same day because ATC will not be available during that period.

The airport said it had arranged staffing to keep its own operations running, while respecting employees’ right to join the demonstration. However, without air traffic control, aircraft cannot operate safely.…
items.t: Belgian strike to disrupt flights at Brussels and Charleroi airports

items.title: Air Niugini B767 diverts to Davao after engine fire warning
items.summary:
An Air Niugini Boeing 767-300ER diverted to the Philippines after the crew received an engine fire indication while en route from Hong Kong to Port Moresby.

The aircraft, registered P2-PXW, landed at Davao International Airport (DVO) shortly after midnight local time. All 137 passengers and nine crew members were reported safe.

Crew shuts down engine at FL330 

The aircraft was operating flight PX19 from Hong Kong International Airport (HKG) to Port Moresby Jacksons International Airport (POM).

According to incident reports , the Boeing 767 was cruising at flight level 330, approximately 160 nautical miles northeast of Davao, when the crew received a fire indication for the right-hand Pratt & Whitney PW4060 engine.

The crew followed the emergency procedures, shut down and secured the affected engine, and diverted to Davao. The aircraft landed on runway 05 at approximately 00:08 a.m. local time on November 21, about 45 minutes after the crew reported the indication.

Air Niugini later confirmed that the crew had shut down the engine before diverting and that the aircraft landed safely.

B767 evacuated after landing 

After landing, the aircraft taxied toward Taxiway 4 and was evacuated using emergency slides. CAAP confirmed that all 146 people on board were safe.

A subsequent assessment reported damage to all four right-side landing gear wheels. The aircraft remained secured at Davao while the incident was investigated.

Davao International Airport was temporarily closed to facilitate emergency response activities and runway safety checks. Two inbound flights from…
items.t: Air Niugini B767 diverts to Davao after engine fire warning

items.title: Russian helicopter suspected of Finnish airspace breach amid drone attack on ship
items.summary:
Finland’s Ministry of Defense said on November 21, 2026, that a Russian helicopter was suspected of violating Finnish airspace off the coastal town of Loviisa, in an incident potentially linked to a drone attack on a Russian cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland earlier the same day.

According to the ministry , the suspected violation occurred at 12:34 local time, with the helicopter penetrating Finnish airspace by as much as 4.1 kilometers (2.5 miles). The ministry did not identify the helicopter type or say how long it remained in Finnish airspace.

Defense Minister Antti Häkkänen said the suspected violation was “possibly related to the rescue or monitoring operations” involving the damaged vessel. He added that the Finnish Defense Forces and Finnish Border Guard were handling the situation in coordination with other authorities. The Border Guard is responsible for investigating the incident.

Drone-hit Russian cargo ship drifts into Finnish waters 

Earlier on November 21, 2026, the Finnish Ministry of Defense reported that the Finnish Defense Forces had detected a drone attack that morning on a Russian cargo ship west of the Russian island of Gogland, known in Finnish as Suursaari, in international waters. The ministry did not identify who carried out the attack.

The Finnish Border Guard, which identified the vessel as Sparta II, said the ship was on fire and had drifted into Finnish territorial waters off Loviisa. The agency is leading the maritime rescue operation, has established a restricted zone around the vessel and has been in contact with Russian maritime rescue…
items.t: Russian helicopter suspected of Finnish airspace breach amid drone attack on ship

items.title: Iraq selling two Boeing 747s stranded in Africa for 35 years for $1.8 million
items.summary:
Iraq is offering two Boeing 747s for sale for a combined $1.8 million after the aircraft spent 35 years parked at an airport in Tunisia, where they were flown for safekeeping ahead of the 1991 Gulf War.

Iraqi Airways published a sale notice on November 18, 2026, valuing each aircraft at $900,000. Companies and individuals can submit offers for either airplane or both. The aircraft remain at Tozeur-Nefta International Airport in southwestern Tunisia.

The pair comprises a Boeing 747-200 registered YI-AGP and a shorter-fuselage 747SP registered YI-ALM. Both were manufactured in 1982. The 747SP served as a government aircraft during Saddam Hussein’s rule.

They were flown to Tunisia in January 1991 as Iraq prepared for coalition air strikes following its invasion of Kuwait. International sanctions, legal disputes and mounting parking charges subsequently complicated efforts to recover them.

The aircraft also became entangled in efforts to recover Kuwaiti property seized during the invasion. A United Nations report documented a September 2005 inspection that found a Kuwait Airways engine installed on the 747-200 and Kuwaiti spare parts aboard both aircraft. Iraqi and Kuwaiti representatives agreed to arrange their return.

Iraq settled approximately $5.4 million in parking fees and other charges with Tunisian authorities in 2020, according to aviation industry publication ch-aviation. The two aircraft remained at the airport.

An earlier sale attempt in 2023 valued each airplane at $494,000. That offering included a condition prohibiting buyers from using the aircraft for…
items.t: Iraq selling two Boeing 747s stranded in Africa for 35 years for $1.8 million

items.title: Archer teams with Disney on aviation research, unveils Avengers-themed air taxi
items.summary:
Archer Aviation has teamed with Walt Disney Imagineering’s research and development arm to explore future transportation concepts, marking the announcement with an Avengers-themed electric aircraft at the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix.

The companies announced the collaboration on November 19, 2026. Archer’s Midnight electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft appeared at the event wearing Disney branding and a custom livery promoting Marvel Studios’ upcoming film Avengers: Doomsday.

Archer described the work with Disney Imagineering as “early, exploratory research,” with the teams planning to examine technical concepts and potential passenger experiences. The announcement provided few details about the projects they intend to pursue or when the research might produce results.

Midnight is designed to carry a pilot and four passengers on short flights, with limited charging time between trips. Archer’s planned services would connect destinations such as city centers and airports, offering travelers a way to avoid congested roads.

The Las Vegas appearance follows Archer’s multiyear agreement with Formula 1, announced on November 12, 2026. Under that partnership, the companies will explore air taxi services for fans, VIP guests and other attendees traveling to and from selected races.

Their plans include looking at dedicated pickup and drop-off locations near circuits and incorporating flights into Formula 1 hospitality and ticket packages. Archer has identified the US, Middle East, Asia and Europe as markets where the partnership could support its planned…
items.t: Archer teams with Disney on aviation research, unveils Avengers-themed air taxi

At a press conference, Kosiniak-Kamysz identified two other suspected impact sites: Rudnik nad Sanem and Mołodycz, both in Podkarpackie Voivodeship. He said the object at Rudnik nad Sanem was also likely a missile, while the one at Mołodycz was probably a jet-powered drone. No injuries or damage to critical infrastructure have been reported.

items.title: Dutch startup Elysian Aircraft raises €12M, enters military research program
items.summary:
On November 19, 2026, Dutch electric aircraft developer Elysian Aircraft announced that it has closed a €12 million pre-Series A funding round. 

Elysian Aircraft will use these funds to further the development of aerospace electrification technologies. 

The current round has been backed by several institutional investors, such as FideFlux, SecFund and ROM InWest, as well as various undisclosed individual investors and family offices. In the press release announcing the latest round, Elysian Aircraft has also hinted that is looking to raise further funds through a Series A in 2027. 

These developments add to a rather eventful month for the electric aircraft industry, which has seen a new €124.5 million raised by Munich-based (Dutch-founded) electric aircraft developer Vaeridion, the first flight of the Chinese CE-25A electric demonstrator as well as the unveiling of the first prototype of ATEA , the hybrid-electric aircraft being developed by French startup Ascendance. 

Until now, the focus of Elysian Aircraft was the development of the E9X , a battery-electric aircraft project. 

The E9X stands out in the electric aircraft scene because of its ambitious goals. Unlike other electric aircraft startups, which have focused on smaller designs for the commuter or regional aircraft markets, Elysian Aircraft is developing the E9X to serve trunk routes currently operated by larger aircraft such as the A320 and B737. The E9X is designed to carry around 90 passengers for distances of up to 1,000 km. 

The development of battery-electric aircraft with this size and range remains…
items.t: Dutch startup Elysian Aircraft raises €12M, enters military research program

items.title: Russia announces third Su-57 fighter delivery of 2026
items.summary:
Rostec, parent company of Russia’s United Aircraft Corporation (UAC), announced that it had delivered another batch of Sukhoi Su-57 fifth-generation fighters to the Russian Aerospace Forces. 

This is the third Su-57 delivery UAC has publicly announced in 2026. As with the previous two, the company did not disclose how many aircraft were handed over. 

According to Rostec, the fighters completed a full cycle of factory tests before Russian Ministry of Defense pilots evaluated them in various flight modes and ferried them to their home base, not identified in the release. 

Upgraded Su-57 weapons and onboard systems 

Rostec highlighted that the aircraft are equipped with upgraded onboard systems and weapons, including “low-observable cruise missiles”. The company did not specify which types. 

UAC presented two air-launched weapons intended for fifth-generation fighters, the S-71K cruise missile and the S-71M autonomous attack weapon, at Egypt’s El Alamein International Airshow in September 2026 . 

An unnamed Su-57 pilot, quoted within the release, said that the aircraft had already performed well in Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, and that the upgrades would expand the range of missions it can perform. 

Open-source assessments indicate that the aircraft has primarily been used to launch stand-off missiles from Russian airspace during the war. 

Russia keeps Su-57 production figures undisclosed 

“The Su-57 is in demand with the troops, so our aircraft plants are not reducing the production pace, and new batches of aircraft are already in production,” Rostec said. 

UAC…
items.t: Russia announces third Su-57 fighter delivery of 2026

items.title: France deploys nuclear-capable Rafales to Sweden for first deterrence drill
items.summary:
Rafale fighters from the French Strategic Air Forces (FAS) were deployed to Sweden from November 16 to 18, 2026, as part of Exercise Excalibur, the first joint exercise under the two countries’ forward deterrence framework, the Swedish Armed Forces announced on November 19, 2026. 

The French aircraft operated alongside Swedish Air Force Gripen fighters in northern Sweden, supported by an Airbus A330 MRTT tanker, according to a separate statement from the French Ministry of the Armed Forces . The exercise aimed to improve interoperability between the two air forces and demonstrate their ability to collaborate. 

Photographs released by the French military show at least three two-seat Rafale B fighters and two Swedish Gripen C fighters. Although neither defense ministry identified the bases used during Excalibur, photographs released by the Swedish Armed Forces show French and Swedish aircrew at Kallax Air Base near Luleå, while flight-tracking data confirms that a French A330 MRTT tanker landed at Luleå-Kallax during the exercise.

The exercise aimed to improve interoperability between the two air forces and demonstrate their ability to operate together. Both countries stressed that no nuclear weapons were involved and that the exercise was not directed at any country.

From Macron’s proposal to joint operations 

A Swedish Gripen fighter flies in formation with French Rafales during Exercise Excalibur. (Credit: État-major des armées) 

The FAS operates the airborne component of France’s nuclear deterrent. French President Emmanuel Macron introduced the concept of forward…
items.t: France deploys nuclear-capable Rafales to Sweden for first deterrence drill

items.title: Turkey inducts KIZILELMA as Baykar delivers first three unmanned fighter jets
items.summary:
Baykar has delivered the first three KIZILELMA unmanned fighter jets to Turkish security forces, as announced by the Turkish drone maker on November 19, 2026.

According to Baykar, the aircraft entered service after completing their acceptance tests, with test and training activities under the program reaching 600 sorties. The company noted that the delivery makes Türkiye the first country to induct an unmanned fighter jet into its inventory.

“Today we are delivering to our nation the dream we built 20 years ago,” Baykar said in a statement posted on its official social media account, in which it also paid tribute to its late founder, Özdemir Bayraktar. Baykar did not specify which branch or unit received the aircraft, referring only to “security forces”.

Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan welcomed the delivery on social media, calling it “a historic day when a great dream became reality”. He declared that the aircraft had joined the inventory of the Turkish Armed Forces “after years of work and great effort”.

items.title: Embraer and Envoy Air extend E-Jet heavy maintenance deal as US MRO demand grows
items.summary:
Embraer announced on November 19, 2026, that it has extended its heavy maintenance agreement with Envoy Air, expanding the scope of the supplemental heavy maintenance it performs on the carrier’s E-Jet fleet.

The work will continue at Embraer’s US maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) facilities in Macon, Georgia, and Fort Worth, Texas, with the expanded scope increasing the capacity Embraer dedicates to Envoy. Financial terms have not been disclosed.

Envoy, a wholly-owned subsidiary of American Airlines Group and American Airlines’ largest regional carrier, operates 189 E-Jets. It continues to take new deliveries from Embraer under a minimum fleet commitment of 214 aircraft.

John Nicks, Envoy’s Senior Vice President of Corporate Services, stressed that the carrier has partnered with Embraer for nearly three decades, and that the agreement provides “supplemental maintenance services to support our growing E-Jet fleet”.

Frank Stevens, Vice President of Global MRO Centers at Embraer Services & Support, described Envoy as one of the world’s largest E-Jet operators and suggested that the deal would help “enhance reliability, maximize aircraft availability and support Envoy’s growth”.

Expanding US maintenance capacity 

The agreement comes as Embraer expands its MRO presence in the United States, where it claims demand is growing among operators seeking maintenance support backed by the original equipment manufacturer (OEM).

In Fort Worth, Embraer is investing about $70 million in a new commercial aviation MRO facility at Perot Field Alliance Airport, due to enter…
items.t: Embraer and Envoy Air extend E-Jet heavy maintenance deal as US MRO demand grows

items.title: Cebu Pacific takes delivery of new A320neo ahead of the Christmas travel rush
items.summary:
With the Philippines’ busiest travel season now just weeks away, Cebu Pacific (CEB) has added another aircraft to its fleet.

The carrier took delivery of an Airbus A320neo on November 19, 2026, its sixth new aircraft of the year and the fourth A320neo to join the fleet during 2026. The aircraft was flown to Manila from Airbus’ final assembly facility in Tianjin, China.

The delivery follows the November 8 arrival of an Airbus A321neo painted in a special livery marking the airline’s 30th anniversary, dubbed the Dreamer Plane.

Cebu Pacific Airbus A321neo Dreamer Plane 

“As we approach the peak holiday travel season, having additional aircraft in our fleet helps us prepare for increased passenger demand,” said Xander Lao, CEB President and Chief Commercial Officer.

Fleet renewal continues 

Lao noted that the new aircraft also reflect the airline’s continued investment in newer-generation jets, “allowing us to grow our capacity while improving fuel efficiency and operational performance”.

Cebu Pacific expects to receive seven NEO aircraft in total this year. NEO models already make up 78% of its jet fleet. According to the airline, they burn 15% to 20% less fuel per flight than previous-generation aircraft and are significantly quieter, cutting both carbon emissions and noise.

The carrier currently operates 15 Airbus A330s, 28 A321s, 39 A320s and 19 ATR turboprops, a mix that it claims gives it the widest network coverage in the Philippines.

Christmas is the Philippines’ peak travel season, typically bringing high passenger demand, elevated fares and added airline…
items.t: Cebu Pacific takes delivery of new A320neo ahead of the Christmas travel rush

items.title: Air New Zealand faces criminal charges over passenger compensation
items.summary:
Air New Zealand faces criminal charges, with the country’s consumer regulator having accused it of misleading passengers about compensation for delayed and canceled flights and rejecting claims that the government body argues it should have paid.

The Commerce Commission announced on November 19, 2026, that it would file charges under the Fair Trading Act in Auckland District Court. Its case concerns statements made directly to passengers seeking compensation for disruptions within the airline’s control.

The regulator alleges that Air New Zealand told passengers their compensation was capped below legal limits and incorrectly restricted the expenses they could claim. The commission said that it believes the misleading statements date back to January 2024.

“Ultimately, we believe passengers missed out on money they were entitled to under the law,” said Commerce Commission Deputy Chair Anne Callinan.

Air New Zealand apologized, but claimed that its own review found the mistakes were neither intentional nor systemic.

“We acknowledge that we didn’t get it right for those customers, and we’re sorry,” said Jeremy O’Brien, the airline’s Chief Customer and Digital Officer.

According to O’Brien, the airline voluntarily reviewed more than 62,000 claims involving disruptions within its control and found errors in fewer than 1% of cases. It stresses having contacted affected customers to resolve the mistakes and reinforcing staff training and guidance on compensation.

The airline stated that it was disappointed the commission had decided to pursue court proceedings given the…
items.t: Air New Zealand faces criminal charges over passenger compensation

items.title: US lawmakers target Airbus contracts over China ties
items.summary:
As US President Donald Trump wrapped up summit talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping, US lawmakers urged the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to refuse certification of Chinese-made aircraft and called for stripping US government contracts from aerospace companies that continue investing in China.

The House Select Committee on China argues that Western aerospace partnerships have helped China to strengthen its military, according to a congressional report published on November 19, 2026. Airbus is among the companies targeted by the proposed contract restrictions. The recommendations would require government action before taking effect.

Airbus’s Chinese partnerships have drawn previous scrutiny from US lawmakers. In a December 2025 letter to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, committee Chairman John Moolenaar questioned whether the European manufacturer’s Chinese partnerships were helping companies involved in military aircraft production.

The letter singled out Xi’an Aircraft Industry Group, which manufactures A320 wings for Airbus’s Tianjin operation and also develops Chinese military aircraft. The committee argued that commercial manufacturing work could give those companies skills and capabilities useful to military programs.

Moolenaar also accused the French government of obstructing the inquiry by controlling what Airbus could disclose to foreign authorities. According to his letter, Airbus had appeared willing to cooperate.

Airbus opened a second A320-family final assembly line in Tianjin in October 2025 under an agreement with the Tianjin Free Trade Zone…

items.title: FAA orders Boeing 737NG checks over loss-of-control risk
items.summary:
The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has ordered repeated checks on certain Boeing 737 Next Generation aircraft, having identified a fault that could prevent an autothrottle safety system from responding to unequal engine thrust, potentially leading to a loss of control.

The airworthiness directive (AD) covers an estimated 300 US-registered aircraft. It is scheduled for publication on November 20, 2026, and takes effect 15 days later.

The problem involves missing or incorrect spoiler-position data used by the autothrottle’s cruise thrust split monitor. Without reliable data, the monitor could fail to activate, allowing a large difference in engine thrust to develop without the autothrottle disengaging.

This could cause the aircraft to roll unexpectedly. If pilots do not recognize and correct the condition promptly, they could lose control, the FAA said.

The agency bypassed the normal advance public-comment process, citing the safety risk. Operators must perform recurring built-in tests of the digital flight control system, correct failures and repeat testing until the system passes.

The directive, AD 2026-23-04, applies to specified 737-600, -700, -700C, -800 and -900 aircraft. It does not cover the 737 MAX.

The FAA addressed a similar concern on older 737 Classic aircraft in October 2022, when it ordered repeated tests on certain 737-300, -400 and -500 models.

In that directive, the agency noted that a failed spoiler sensor could go undetected by the autothrottle computer. A review found that maintenance testing was needed to identify failures involving the…
items.t: FAA orders Boeing 737NG checks over loss-of-control risk

items.title: In pictures: Ascendance unveils full-scale ATEA hybrid-electric VTOL
items.summary:
French startup Ascendance unveiled the full-scale prototype of its ATEA hybrid-electric vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) aircraft on November 19, 2026, as the Toulouse-based company prepares for its flight-test campaign.

The unveiling follows the completion of the demonstrator’s airframe, which Ascendance announced on February 23, 2026. The structure was manufactured by Duqueine Group in Lyon, France, under Ascendance’s engineering direction, clearing the way for the integration of the propulsion system, avionics, and fly-by-wire flight controls.

Speaking to the media during the unveiling event, which took place at Muret-Lherm airfield near Toulouse, Ascendance co-founder Jean-Cristophe Lambert, highlighted also the strategic significance of the ATEA program, as the first European aircraft developed from scratch around a hybrid-electric architecture. Lambert referred to the need for Europe to strengthen its industrial autonomy in aerospace and defense and pointed out that the ATEA has been built mostly with European components and technology.

Ascendance has raised €60 million so far, a figure that Lambert acknowledged, is relatively small in comparison to the amounts raised by some eVTOL developers in the United States and China. This, however, has not prevented the French startup from making major progress to date, stated Lambert, taking pride in the efficient use of resources.

Ascendance expects the first flight of the ATEA prototype to take place at some point in early 2027, as soon as the company gets permission from the aviation authority to start its flight…
items.t: In pictures: Ascendance unveils full-scale ATEA hybrid-electric VTOL

items.title: US firms seek new 250-mile speed lane for supersonic-hypersonic flight tests
items.summary:
A group of US companies are looking to establish a new 250-mile speed corridor between Texas and New Mexico as a supersonic and hypersonic flight test facility.

On November 18, 2026, the four members, which includes two FAA -licensed spaceports, signed a letter of intent (LOI) to “jointly define, advocate for, and develop a dedicated high-speed flight test corridor”.

Midland Development Corporation, Midland International Air & Space Port, the New Mexico Spaceport Authority, operator of Spaceport America, and Starfighters Space said the “proposal comes as federal regulators consider easing overland supersonic flight restrictions and expanding US space launch capacity”.

The group argue that if successful, the 250-mile corridor between Midland International Air & Space Port in West Texas and Spaceport America in southern New Mexico could support repeatable, high-cadence supersonic and hypersonic flight research including sonic boom overpressure measurement and air traffic integration procedure development.

Spaceport America 

The test corridor would also provide real-world flight data to help shape evolving supersonic flight and space launch regulations.

“A long-term goal of the corridor is to one day support operations to and above the Kármán line for suborbital and orbital launch, air launch, point-to-point spaceflight, and the reentry and recovery of spaceflight vehicles and payloads,” the group added.

The LOI follows two federal actions now before the FAA. Firstly, a rulemaking for the removal of the longstanding prohibition on overland flight above Mach 1 with a…
items.t: US firms seek new 250-mile speed lane for supersonic-hypersonic flight tests

items.title: Inside Thales’ plan to keep Asia-Pacific’s fast-growing airline fleets airborne
items.summary:
With Asia-Pacific expected to remain one of the world’s fastest-growing aviation regions through 2050, Thales is betting that the airlines flying there will want two things from their maintenance partners. Firstly, that parts be close by and secondly, that those parts will be ready when needed.

Thomas Got, Managing Director of Aviation Global Services at Thales, spoke to AeroTime in an exclusive interview at the company’s booth during MRO Asia-Pacific 2026 in Singapore.

He described a strategy built on local presence, guaranteed parts availability and long-term partnerships, including a recent agreement with Vietjet.

Got, who was recently named a Knight of the National Order of Merit in France for his contributions to the defense and aerospace industries, has spent much of his career in those sectors, including work modernizing air surveillance and air defense systems.

He now oversees Thales’ aviation services business, where Asia-Pacific is a key growth market.

“The region is fast growing, probably the fastest-growing area worldwide,” Got said. “So for us, it’s very important to be well present in this market. It’s a question of bringing capabilities close to our customers.”

A three-hub footprint across Singapore, Beijing and New Delhi 

Thales runs its regional operations from a headquarters in Singapore, with additional sites in Beijing and New Delhi. The New Delhi facility, located near the city’s airport, opened in 2025.

Got explained the expansion reflects the company’s view that serving airlines in a region this large requires being physically present in its…
items.t: Inside Thales’ plan to keep Asia-Pacific’s fast-growing airline fleets airborne

items.title: Hanwha Systems wins first US contract for counter-drone radar
items.summary:
Hanwha Systems has secured its first radar export contract in the US, agreeing to supply short-range active electronically scanned array (AESA) radars to US defense technology company Rebellion Industries. 

The agreement is a pilot export deal, under which a small number of radars will initially be delivered to assess their suitability for the US market. Neither company disclosed the number of units ordered or the contract value. 

Hanwha said deliveries would take place in stages through early 2027. The two companies are also discussing follow-on contracts for larger orders in the US. 

Hanwha and Rebellion target US counter-drone market  

Under the agreement, Hanwha and Rebellion plan to integrate the South Korean company’s radar with Rebellion’s Sensor OS software to develop a counter-drone platform for military and civilian applications. 

According to Hanwha, the radars will initially be deployed at civilian infrastructure sites in the US, including oil refineries, corporate data centers, logistics centers and stadiums. 

Rebellion Industries, led by founder and CEO Shu Chowdhury, develops technology for detecting and responding to threats against critical infrastructure. Its product portfolio includes software that combines radar, electro-optical and other sensor data into a single operational picture, as well as its own compact AESA radar, called ARGUS. 

Compact AESA radar designed to detect low-flying drones  

The radar covered by the contract has a detection range of 10 kilometers (6.2 miles) and is designed primarily to detect and track drones and other small…
items.t: Hanwha Systems wins first US contract for counter-drone radar

items.title: F-35C completes first Ford-class carrier trials aboard John F. Kennedy
items.summary:
Two F-35C Lightning II fighters have completed the first launch and recovery trials aboard a Gerald R. Ford-class aircraft carrier, marking a step toward integrating the US Navy’s carrier-based stealth fighter with its newest warships.

The tests took place aboard the future USS John F. Kennedy (CVN 79), the second Ford-class carrier, over an 11-day period, Lockheed Martin announced on November 19, 2026.

According to the manufacturer, two F-35Cs from Naval Air Station Patuxent River, Maryland, completed 122 catapult launches and 122 arrested landings in 34 flights during the campaign.

The first F-35C arrested landing aboard Kennedy took place on October 13, 2026, coinciding with the US Navy’s 251st birthday. Lockheed Martin did not specify the start and end dates of the full test period.

Testing the F-35C with Ford-class launch and recovery systems 

Unlike the older Nimitz-class carriers, which use steam-powered catapults, Ford-class ships employ the Electromagnetic Aircraft Launch System (EMALS) and Advanced Arresting Gear (AAG). These systems are designed to provide greater control over aircraft launches and recoveries.

The Ford class also features a redesigned flight deck and island, creating a different operating environment for aircraft and deck crews.

During the trials, engineers gathered data to verify the EMALS and AAG software and installations, assess the loads imposed on the F-35C during launches and landings, and validate the aircraft’s structural models.

The results will also support the development of aircraft launch and recovery bulletins, which…
items.t: F-35C completes first Ford-class carrier trials aboard John F. Kennedy

items.title: UK defense plan under fire as BAE Systems looks to cut 1,070 jobs
items.summary:
The UK’s defense plan has come under fire after British firm BAE Systems announced plans to cut 1,070 jobs, including 940 roles from within its air division.

The development comes as BAE Systems said it is looking to “reduce complexity, improve efficiency and ensure every pound invested delivers maximum value and capability back to defense”.

Following the announcement on November 18, 2026, the union Unite blamed delays in UK defense spending for “driving companies in the sector to make negative decisions impacting British jobs”.

“In order to stop the erosion of defense jobs and get the growth we need, the government needs to announce contracts for British built Typhoons and Collaborative Combat Aircraft immediately,” Unite General Secretary Sharon Graham said.

Edgewing 

In September 2025, Turkey ordered 20 Eurofighter Typhoon fighter jets from the UK, however this project is unlikely to sustain long-term job prospects.

On November 19, 2026, the Shadow Minister for Defence Procurement, Ben Obese-Jecty, said that if the Labour government does not support the industry with orders, then it “will simply go where the orders are”.

“The Government talks a good game on defense and resilience, but the reality doesn’t match rhetoric,” Obese-Jecty wrote. “As the rest of Europe rearms, the Government remains paralyzed by indecision.”

In a statement, BAE Systems said it had spoken with staff about the company’s “ongoing focus on enhancing our agility and competitiveness”.

“We are at an early stage in this process and will now enter into a period of consultation as we develop…
items.t: UK defense plan under fire as BAE Systems looks to cut 1,070 jobs

items.title: SITA’s Sumesh Patel on how Asia-Pacific airports can handle more with less space
items.summary:
Current predictions suggest that Asia-Pacific will account for almost half of the world’s future passenger growth – but its airports won’t be able to double in size to keep up. 

For SITA (Société Internationale de Télécommunications Aéronautiques), the solution lies in moving passengers, bags and borders through the same space more quickly, and in moving more of the airport journey away from the airport itself.

At Passenger Terminal Expo Asia 2026 in Singapore, AeroTime sat down with Sumesh Patel, President for Asia Pacific at SITA, the air transport IT provider, to discuss biometric borders, baggage tracking and how the region is preparing for a future of up to 10 billion passengers a year.

Patel said the timing of the expo’s first edition in Asia reflected where the industry is heading. “When we look at the airlines, the airports, the expansion – the future growth in terms of the passenger is in Asia,” he said, adding that the event had been busier than he expected.

Border Flow: from ‘stop and check’ to ‘walk through’ 

SITA launched its Border Flow lane as a commercial product on September 9, 2026, after trialing the concept for years at its customer experience center in Singapore.

The system pre-clears passengers before they reach the airport, enabling them to walk through border control without stopping. SITA claims to process travelers up to eight times faster than traditional e-gates, with 75% of travelers cleared before departure.

According to Patel, the benefits go both ways. Passengers no longer queue at gates or counters, while immigration officers can…
items.t: SITA’s Sumesh Patel on how Asia-Pacific airports can handle more with less space

items.title: Belgium pledges 10 F-16s, France two Mirage jets for Ukraine by end of 2026
items.summary:
Ukraine’s allies announced plans to deliver 10 Belgian F-16 fighters and two French Mirage 2000-5F jets by the end of 2026, alongside additional air defense missiles, radars and ammunition, at the 37th meeting of the Ukraine Defense Contact Group (UDCG). 

The commitments, published by Ukraine’s Ministry of Defense on November 18, 2026, followed a meeting at NATO headquarters in Brussels the day before. Several countries also pledged new funding for the Prioritized Ukraine Requirements List (PURL) , through which allies finance US-made weapons for Kyiv. 

“This winter, our biggest priority is protecting the skies,” Ukrainian Defense Minister Yevhenii Khmara said, according to the ministry. 

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who addressed the meeting remotely, called for the provision of 40 additional F-16 fighters . He said Ukraine’s existing jets spend considerable time undergoing maintenance and repairs, limiting their availability for combat missions. 

UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting and German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius co-chaired the session. 

Defense ministers and representatives of Ukraine’s allies attend the 37th meeting of the Ukraine Defense Contact Group at NATO headquarters in Brussels, Belgium. (Credit: NATO) 

UK, Germany and Nordic allies reinforce Ukraine’s air defenses 

The UK announced a £240 million (about $316 million) package that includes more than 1,000 short-range air defense missiles and launchers, along with more than a dozen radars. 

The missiles include Lightweight Multirole Missiles (LMM), manufactured by Thales in Belfast.…
items.t: Belgium pledges 10 F-16s, France two Mirage jets for Ukraine by end of 2026
